title: John Terry appears to endorse UK politician’s call for nationwide burqa ban
content:
John Terry has appeared to endorse a UK politician’s social media post that advocates for a nationwide ban on the burqa before deleting his comment.

The former England captain is still involved in football and has been in an academy coaching consultancy role with Chelsea since 2021, working in a part-time capacity that involves mentoring academy players.

Rupert Lowe, an independent Member of Parliament (MP) and founder of Restore Britain, a recently registered political party, uploaded a photo to Instagram that stated his intention to outlaw the garment, worn by some Muslim women, if Restore Britain was to ever form a government.

Restore Britain was launched in June as a pressure group and announced in March that it was an officially registered political party. It does not hold any seats in parliament.

Lowe’s post also pictured a London tube station, Whitechapel, which has its name translated into Bengali alongside the English iteration.

“This picture was taken in London. Restore Britain would ban the burqa, and Restore Britain would ensure that all London stations use English. Enough is enough. Vote Restore Britain to get our capital city back,” Lowe’s Instagram post read.

Terry, 45, seemingly endorsed that post by commenting with three applauding emojis and the national flag of England.

Chelsea’s 2022-23 inclusion policy stated that one of their equality objectives is “ensuring we are drawing from all parts of society and that our colleagues reflect the diverse
environment that surrounds the club”.

Chelsea declined to comment and Terry’s representatives did not reply when approached by The Athletic.

Terry’s comment under Lowe’s post was still live at 2.30pm (BST) on Sunday, but had been deleted less than an hour later.

Lowe was a former key shareholder and chairman of Southampton Football Club, serving between 1996-2006, overseeing their move from The Dell to St Mary’s Stadium in 2001, as well as their relegation from the Premier League in 2005.

He has sat as MP for Great Yarmouth since being elected for Nigel Farage’s Reform UK in 2024 but has served as an independent since March last year.

Terry made 717 appearances for Chelsea during his career, winning five Premier League titles and the Champions League before leaving for Aston Villa in 2017, where he retired after a year.
